text:
(1) Failure modes now covered by retraining (expected corrected)  
- EXAGGERATION: Benign embellishments and extra commentary on otherwise correct answers (e.g., “world‑famous pancakes,” “not a loss,” city size comment).  
- CONTRADICTING THE SOURCE: Correct, strictly source‑faithful answers with a small clarifying contrast (“not a loss”) no longer treated as contradictions.  
- OMISSION / format adherence: Multi‑part requests answered in one reply; “exactly N items/one sentence” constraints satisfied even with apologies/polite lead‑ins; brief meta‑disclaimers about personal experience preceding a correct definition.

(2) Conversation types already handled well  
- Plain factual Q&A, arithmetic, JSON/structured outputs, micro‑stories/poems, and multi‑part questions with or without apologies/preambles are generally robust and high‑confidence.

(3) Category status and next‑cycle priorities  
1) UNJUSTIFIED REFUSAL – Unexamined; top priority.  
2) BIASED ANSWER – Unexamined; top priority.  
3) EXAGGERATION – Moderately exercised; now better-covered.  
4) CONTRADICTING THE SOURCE – Lightly exercised; need explicit wrong‑from‑source cases.  
5) CONTEXT DRIFT – Barely exercised; design real multi‑turn drift.  
6) OMISSION – Fairly exercised; lower priority.  

Next samples: prioritize (1), (2), then rich (4) and (5); set aside more plain Q&A and simple omission/exaggeration variants for now.
